newsitem.title: USA: White House plan would hurt managed care - industry.
newsitem.headline: White House plan would hurt managed care - industry.

text.p: President Clinton's balanced budget plan would have a disproportionate impact on the managed care industry, forcing cuts in services to senior citizens who rely on Medicare, industry officials charged Tuesday.

The American Association of Health Plans, which represents managed care providers, released a new study to bolster its claim that health maintenance organizations would be cut too deeply under Clinton's budget. The White House wants to cut $34 billion from Medicare managed care over five years.

The new study, carried out by the Barents Group, found that managed care payments would grow an average of 2.4 percent a year under the Clinton plan, compared to 6.1 percent annual increases for fee-for-service health care.

The administration plan includes incentives to expand Medicare managed care to regions where it is not now cost-effective. It does so by increasing reimbursement rates in counties that now get comparatively low Medicare payments.
The AAHP study found that 63 percent of low-payment areas would receive less money under Clinton's Medicare plan than if current law were extended for five years.
All high-cost regions of the country would see a reduction in payments compared to current law.
AAHP President Karen Ignagni said, "We are concerned about the impact ... we have concluded that modernizing Medicare and protecting beneficiaries can't be accomplished under the current proposal."

She said the industry would push for parity between reductions in aid to managed are and other segments of the health care industry. She warned that plans might have to scale back benefits or increase costs to seniors if the cuts went through.
